title: Microsoft Research Asia has released Agent Lightning v1.0, a small open-source tool that trains AI agents using the software they actually run.
key_facts: Microsoft Research Asia open-sourced a rebuilt Agent Lightning v1.0 of about 3,500 lines of code.
The framework has three parts: an API Gateway, a Rollout Controller and a Customized Trainer built on verl.
It works with existing agent software such as mini-SWE-agent, OpenHands, Claude Code and Codex by pointing the model endpoint at its proxy.
In experiments, Collocated Async RL was about 2x faster end to end than synchronous RL.
RL training raised Qwen3.5-9B from 41.8% to 56.4% on SWE-bench Verified, using about 6,000 training samples.
The result is the team's own; the article shows no outside review.
quote_evidence: RL training alone raised Qwen3.5-9B from 41.8% to 56.4% on SWE-bench Verified, a gain of 14.6 percentage points.
The entire framework is about 3,500 lines of code, with three core components: the API Gateway, the Rollout Controller, and the Customized Trainer (Figure 2).
why_it_matters_hint: Training coding agents with the same software they are deployed with could make trained agents behave as expected, but the gains are one team's test.
notes: Full text read. Preliminary: early research result with no outside review in the text.
